tips.title: Use PETG plastic sheets for durability and versatility
tips.text: PETG (Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol) plastic sheets are an excellent choice for scale modeling due to their durability, flexibility, and resistance to scratches and cuts. They can be easily molded, bent, and shaped to create complex designs and details. Brands like Makrolon or Lucite offer high-quality PETG sheets.

tips.title: Select a suitable adhesive for the job, such as cyanoacrylate or epoxy
tips.text: For bonding plastic or resin parts, use a cyanoacrylate-based adhesive like Tamiya's Extra Thin or a two-part epoxy like J-B Weld. For bonding metal or wood, use a epoxy-based adhesive like Loctite's Epoxy Instant Mix.

tips.title: Prime your model with a high-build primer for even coverage and strength
tips.text: Use a high-build primer like Tamiya's HS or Vallejo's Game Color Primer to create a smooth, even surface for painting. These primers also help to strengthen the model and prevent chipping or cracking.

tips.title: Source materials from specialty stores or online retailers for a wide selection
tips.text: Visit specialty stores like HobbyTown or Michaels, or online retailers like Amazon or eBay to find a wide selection of scale modeling materials and supplies. These stores often carry a variety of brands and products, including hard-to-find or specialized items.

tips.title: Store your materials and supplies in a dry, cool, and well-ventilated area
tips.text: Store your scale modeling materials and supplies in a dry, cool, and well-ventilated area to prevent damage from moisture, heat, or chemicals. Avoid storing materials in direct sunlight or near heat sources, and keep them away from children and pets.
